record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: If f and 1/f belong to the Bergman space A2 , does it follow that Pf is dense in A2 ? Here Pf denotes the set of all polynomial multiples of f , i.e. Pf = {pf : p a polynomial}. More generally, if f ∈ A2 and |f (z)| ≥ c(1 − |z|)a for some a, c > 0, then does it follow that Pf is dense in A2 ? (For partial results in this direction, see [4]). (A. L. Shields)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $A^2=A^2(\mathbb{D})$ be the Bergman space of all holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ with
$$\|f\|_{A^2}^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. For $f\in A^2$, set
$$\mathcal{P}f=\{pf : p\text{ is a polynomial}\}\subset A^2.$$
A function $f\in A^2$ is called cyclic (for the operator of multiplication by $z$) if $\mathcal{P}f$ is dense in $A^2$.

(a) Suppose $f\in A^2$ and $1/f\in A^2$ (so in particular $f$ has no zeros in $\mathbb{D}$). Must $\mathcal{P}f$ be dense in $A^2$?

(b) More generally, suppose $f\in A^2$ and there exist constants $a,c>0$ such that
$$|f(z)|\ge c\,(1-|z|)^a\quad\text{for all }z\in\mathbb{D}.$$
Must $\mathcal{P}f$ be dense in $A^2$?
artifact.status_search_result: Borichev and Hedenmalm (J. Amer. Math. Soc., 1997, "Harmonic functions of maximal growth: invertibility and cyclicity in Bergman spaces") constructed a function $f\in A^2(\mathbb{D})$ with $1/f\in A^2(\mathbb{D})$ that is not cyclic, giving a negative answer to (a) and hence to the more general (b). This was extended by Borichev–Hedenmalm–Volberg (2003) to a wide class of weighted Bergman spaces, where invertible non-cyclic elements exist.

status_evidence.title: Large Bergman spaces: invertibility, cyclicity, and subspaces of arbitrary index
status_evidence.snippet: In a wide class of weighted Bergman spaces, we construct invertible non-cyclic elements.
status_evidence.claim: There exists f in A^2 with 1/f in A^2 but f not cyclic, refuting Shields' question.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Borichev and Hedenmalm showed that there is f in L^2_a(D) with 1/f in L^2_a(D) but f not cyclic.
status_evidence.claim: Negative resolution of Shields' problem on cyclicity of invertible Bergman functions.
